arguments.summary: A replay of a prior Cobalt Strike detection on host WS-ENG-015 was attempted, but investigation revealed a critical misattribution. The original action quarantined a host based on malware detection, but replay context indicated a phishing campaign. Further analysis confirmed the presence of Cobalt Strike Beacon via sandboxing. The host WS-ENG-015 was not the source of the initial network scan; instead, the IP 10.0.12.15 was incorrectly associated with WS-ENG-015. The actual system at that IP is WS-IT-101, an Ubuntu machine. The malicious activity originated from a different host. The Admin phase failed to execute containment due to lack of consensus and invalid targeting.

timeline.description: Original incident (INC-2026-0555) action: Host WS-ENG-015 quarantined due to Cobalt Strike beacon detection.
Network scan from external IP 192.168.1.100 detected targeting 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Blocked by IDS.
Normal login to WS-IT-101 by CORP\helpdesk.
Replay initiated for INC-2026-0612. Misattribution identified: IP 10.0.12.15 linked to WS-ENG-015 is incorrect. Actual host at 10.0.2.15 is WS-IT-101 (Ubuntu).
EDR query on WS-ENG-015 shows Chrome process connecting to 142.250.80.46 (Google). No immediate malicious indicators on host.

Sandbox analysis confirms file with hash a1b2c3d4... is Cobalt Strike Beacon (malicious). IOCs extracted: C2 IP 198.51.100.23, domain c2.update-service.xyz, mutex Global\MSCTF.Asm.{b1e5}, file path %TEMP%\beacon.dll, registry key HKCU\Run\SysUpdate.
SIEM search reveals no direct logs linking WS-ENG-015 to the C2. Suspicion shifts to potential lateral movement or misconfiguration.
Admin phase attempts quarantine and firewall block failed due to lack of consensus and incorrect target validation.
